feature.name: Positively exposed descending connector at the upper-to-lower transition
feature.single_categorical_rule: For an observationally bound complete focal construction, assign TRUE when the upper rounded body visibly issues into an exposed descending stroke before the lower turn/body: paper separates the lower departure from the bulk of the upper body and the descent is positively visible outside a common waist. Assign FALSE only when the observed upper and lower rounded bodies meet directly at a shared ink waist/pinch, with both bodies visibly issuing from that same constricted junction. Otherwise assign UNKNOWN.
positive_TRUE_criteria: Bind upper body, descending continuation, and lower turn to the same focal construction.
See a descending stroke exposed below/outside the upper body, with adjoining paper showing its departure from the upper body bulk.
Observe the lower continuation/turn sufficiently to distinguish this departure from a neighbor or clipped unrelated fragment.
negative_FALSE_criteria: Bind both rounded bodies to one complete focal construction.
Positively see a shared constricted ink waist where the upper and lower bodies meet.
The transition is accounted for by that common waist; FALSE is not inferred merely from failure to see a connector.
UNKNOWN_criteria: Focal identity or extent is unresolved, or transition/lower continuation is clipped.
Ink, watermark, neighbor overlap, fading, or resolution prevents a positive distinction.
Both shared-waist and exposed-descent interpretations remain plausible.
excluded_decision_requirements: No exact loop closure or pixel-connectedness requirement.
No measured length, gap width, coordinate cutoff, ratio, or numeric classifier threshold.
No arbitrary division of a curve into segments.
No source shape interpreted as a readable value.
No second feature, substitute feature, or fallback class guessing.
feature.association_basis: C08-E01 visibly demonstrates TRUE; C04-E01 visibly demonstrates FALSE. Association is limited to these actual approved training examples.

categorical_rule.name: positively_exposed_descending_connector
categorical_rule.TRUE: The bound focal ink visibly leaves the upper rounded body on a descending course that remains exposed as a connection toward the lower return. Paper beside that course and the visible continuation establish a passage below the upper body before the lower return, rather than a common local waist between adjacent rounded bodies. Require affirmative ink and paper evidence; apparent missing closure is not evidence.
categorical_rule.FALSE: The bound focal upper and lower rounded bodies affirmatively converge at the same local waist/pinch. The visible ink and adjacent paper place the change from upper body to lower body at that shared junction, without an exposed descending passage between them. Mere failure to see a connector is insufficient.
categorical_rule.UNKNOWN: Use UNKNOWN if focal binding is uncertain, the transition or relevant continuation is clipped/occluded, neighboring ink or watermark cannot be excluded, a shared pinch and an exposed connector remain competing readings, or neither categorical geometry is affirmatively visible. Do not resolve UNKNOWN by apparent closure, quantified length/width, loop counts, angle cutoffs, or selecting arbitrary subcurves.
